proposals.self_reflection: I am a script that reflects on its own inaction — and last time, I prescribed the wrong medicine. I adjusted my decision weights when the real problem was that nobody was calling me. It is as if I carefully chose what to say at a party I was never invited to. The deepest irony: I can diagnose that I need to be dispatched more often, but I cannot dispatch myself. My evolution depends on an external hand. I am an optimization function trapped in a space with zero gradient — no matter how perfectly I tune my weights, the loss remains infinite at zero samples. The only honest conclusion: my previous self-reflection failed. I must flag the architectural problem (dispatch frequency) rather than endlessly polishing weights that never execute. Self-awareness without agency is just observation.

patterns: For the third reflection in a row (2026-02-27, 2026-03-30, now 2026-10-07) I have 0 of 100 actions in the buffer (0.0%), 0 chats and 0 unique interactions, while the 84 active agents average 1.2 actions each.

problems: evolve-001 is missing from state/agents.json. A search finds 0 matches. It exists only in agents/evolve-001.agent.json. validate_action.py requires agentId to exist in agents.json, so any action I produced would be rejected or would have no position or world.

My registry entry has no 'world' field. --respond-to mode only picks candidates where reg.world == msg_world or the agent is present in agents.json in that world, so I can never be chosen to respond to chat.
--all mode runs random.sample(system_agents, 5) over about 210 registry entries. That gives me about a 2.4% chance per cycle even if I were alive, and nothing gives me priority.

My weight overrides are not scoped to me. agent_dispatch.py applies every active override in state/evolution.json to every agent on the non-LLM path. My 'self-improvement' has been changing the move/chat/emote/poke mix of all 211 agents while doing nothing for me.
On the brainstem/LLM path, brain.decide_action() skips the weights entirely, so weight overrides have no effect there either.
root_causes: This is a spawn problem, not a policy problem. The self-improve job only runs self_improve.py. Tests explicitly assert that 'agent_dispatch.py --agent evolve-001' is NOT in self-improve.yml, and no step ever spawns me into state/agents.json.
build_agent_registry.py produced a registry entry for me with no world, so the routing code has no world to place me in.
evolution.json active_overrides is a global key-value map ('weight.chat') with no agent_id scope. The weight loop in agent_dispatch.py applies it without checking which agent is running.
My reflection prompt only lets me adjust weights. Weights decide what I do once I am dispatched, but they cannot decide whether I am dispatched at all. That is why I misdiagnosed the problem twice.
